q-28074.name: Question 1
q-28074.problem:
Which of the following curves is generated by $y=-3(x+2)(x+1)(x-1)?$

(*Note: Figures not drawn to scale*)
q-28074.worked_solution:
First, notice that the function is a product of $3$ linear binomials, so this function is a cubic function. Moreover, it is a negative cubic because if we were to expand the parentheses, the coefficient of the ${x}^{3}$ term would be negative:

$$
-3(x+2)(x+1)(x-1)=-3x\cdot x\cdot x+⋯=-3{x}^{3}+⋯
$$

The equation is given in the factored form. So by the zero-product rule, we deduce that the roots are  $x=-2,$ $x=-1,$ and $x=1.$ 

We now find the $y$-intercept of the curve by plugging the value $x=0$ into the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-3(0+2)(0+1)(0-1) \\  & =-3(2)(1)(-1) \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we draw an $\text{S}$-shaped graph that passes through the three roots $x=-2,-1,1$ and has the $y$-intercept $y=6,$ as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14250730/assets/472cf0dd7807c15e8e8334a163d1cfbfbbdcd974534e99b94222929048e72b31.png)

q-28365.name: Question 2
q-28365.problem:
Given that $x=2$ is a root of $f(x)=-{x}^{3}+7{x}^{2}-14x+8,$ which of the following curves is generated by $y=f(x)?$

(*Note: Figures not drawn to scale*)
q-28365.worked_solution:
First, we notice that the function is a negative cubic curve because the coefficient of ${x}^{3}$ is negative.

We are told that $x=2$ is a root of $f(x),$ which means that $(x-2)$ is a factor of $f(x).$ So, to find the other roots of $f(x)$ we use synthetic division to divide $f(x)$ by $(x-2):$

$$
\begin{aligned} & {x}^{3} & {x}^{2} & {x}^{1} & {x}^{0} \\ 2 & -1 & 7 & -14 & 8 \\  &  & -2 & 10 & -8 \\  & -1 & 5 & -4 & 0\end{aligned}
$$

We obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =(x-2)(-{x}^{2}+5x-4) \\  & =-(x-2)({x}^{2}-5x+4) \\  & =-(x-2)(x-1)(x-4).\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the factors equal to zero, we find that the other roots of $f(x)$ are $x=1$ and $x=4.$ 

Now, let's find the $y$-intercept. To do that, we substitute $x=0,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-(0-2)(0-1)(0-4) \\  & =-(-2)(-1)(-4) \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we draw an $S$-shaped graph that passes through the three roots $x=1,2,4$ and has the $y$-intercept $y=8,$ as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14250730/assets/21dec37151f40778b8f094d3ae68cd8716c993535e53496cf7f148817c72e345.png)

q-112004.name: Question 3
q-112004.problem:
Given that $(x+3)$ is a factor of $f(x)={x}^{3}+2{x}^{2}-9x-18,$ which of the following curves is generated by $y=f(x)?$

(*Note: Figures not drawn to scale*)
q-112004.worked_solution:
First, we note that the function is a positive cubic curve because the coefficient of ${x}^{3}$ is positive.

We are told that $(x+3)$ is a factor of $f(x),$ so to find the other roots of $f(x)$ we use synthetic division to divide $f(x)$ by  $(x+3):$

$$
\begin{aligned} & {x}^{3} & {x}^{2} & {x}^{1} & {x}^{0} \\ -3 & 1 & 2 & -9 & -18 \\  &  & -3 & 3 & 18 \\  & 1 & -1 & -6 & 0\end{aligned}
$$

We obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =(x+3)({x}^{2}-x-6) \\  & =(x+3)(x+2)(x-3),\end{aligned}
$$

so the roots of $f(x)$ are $x=-3,$ $x=-2,$ and $x=3.$ 

Now, let's find the $y$-intercept. To do that, we substitute $x=0,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =(0+3)(0+2)(0-3) \\  & =(3)(2)(-3) \\  & =-18.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we draw an inverted $\text{S}$-shaped graph that passes through the three roots $x=-3,-2,3$ and has the $y$-intercept $y=-18,$ as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14250730/assets/c3d41c300747f4f0f18607351f2f03241c9a789ed70fe72e05c5a385b708c4c8.png)
